references.text: Direct narrative connection: Judah transforms the brothers' collective offer (v.9) into an individual sacrifice (v.33) to save Benjamin.
Narrative context: 43:13 is the command to bring the brother, while 44:33 is the solution that ensures the brother can actually leave.
Theological parallel: Substitution and brotherhood; Judah offers himself as a slave for his brother (Gen), while Onesimus becomes a free brother in the Lord (Philemon).
Direct narrative link: Joseph establishes the rule of one slave (v.17), and Judah fulfills it by taking the place himself (v.33).
